SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-020 (1) To install the attendant or lavatory service unit, do this task: Attendant/Lavatory Service Unit - Installation, TASK 25-23-13-400-801. SUBTASK 25-23-61-860-025 (2) Make sure that the generator release cable is put through the triangular cable window of the mask box. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-021 NOTE: Prior to installing PSU, verify that the chemical oxygen generator is secured with clamps that have pads that are NOT installed with Pressure Sensitive Adhesive (PSA). The incorrect PSA pad material is identified as a pad that is flat and adhered to the inside surface of the clamp. The correct, non-PSA pad material is identified by having channel features that wrap the edges of the clamp to keep them secured. (3) Install the PSU: (a) Locate the correct placement for the PSU type. NOTE: There are several types of PSU's. The location of the PSU types can be different on each plane. NOTE: For PSU location and position data (LH or RH), refer to AIPC 25-23-61. (b) Put the panel in the correct position. (c) Engage latches to PSU rail. 1) Make sure that the pins are engaged. NOTE: You may have to wiggle the panel slightly to ensure pins are engaged. 25-23-61 (d) Let the PSU hang freely from the outboard side (e) Install the flexible air duct to the manifold. (f) Connect the clamp to the flexible duct. (g) Do this task to connect the breathable oxygen lines: Oxygen System General Maintenance Practices, TASK 35-00-00-910-801. (h) Connect the electrical connector. SUBTASK 25-23-61-440-002 (4) Do this task: Oxygen Generator Activation, TASK 35-22-11-400-811-001. SUBTASK 25-23-61-860-019 (5) Make sure that the CALL SELECT switch is put in the same position as the removed CALL SELECT switch as follows: NOTE: You can get access to the passenger CALL SELECT switch when the PSU is lowered. Usually, the passenger CALL SELECT switch is near the passenger reading light assembly. (a) For the PSU in the first class, make sure that the CALL SELECT switch is set in the FWD position and otherwise the CALL SELECT switch is set in the AFT position. (b) For the airplanes with the single class, make sure that the front half of the CALL SELECT switch is put in the FWD position and back half of the CALL SELECT switch is put in the AFT position. SUBTASK 25-23-61-410-002 (6) Do these steps to close the PSU: (a) Connect the lanyard to the PSU rail. (b) Push the PSU up until you hear the latch or latches engage in the PSU rail. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE PSU LATCHES ARE ENGAGED. IF YOU DO NOT CORRECTLY ENGAGE THE LATCHES, THE PSU CAN FALL AND CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (c) If there is more than one latch, lightly pull down on the edges of the PSU to make sure that the latches are engaged. 4. Fixed PSU Spacer Panel Removal Figure 401

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-009 (1) Lower the adjacent spacer panel or Passenger Service Unit (PSU). SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-010 (2) Push in the latch extension of the spring latches and pull downward on the panel bases until all the latches disengage from the PSU rail. SUBTASK 25-23-61-020-013 (3) Lower the inboard edge of the spacer panel while you pull out the outboard hook attachment of the panel from the beam detail air extrusion.

25-23-61-400-806Fixed PSU Spacer Panel InstallationPDF p. 462

5. Fixed PSU Spacer Panel Installation Figure 401

A. General

(1) A fixed spacer panel can be of the widths that follow: (a) 2 inch (b) 6 inch (c) 8 inch (d) 10 inch.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-028 (1) Select and install the spacer panel of the necessary width to close any gap with adjacent Passenger Service Unit (PSU) panels. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-026 (2) Put the outboard hook attachments of the spacer panels into the beam detail air extrusion holes. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-027 (3) Push the inboard edge of the spacer panel upward until the spring latches engage the PSU rail. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-029 (4) Apply upward pressure to the panel base under the spring latches to fully engage the latches. NOTE: The latches will make a “click” sound when fully engaged.

SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-012 (2) Push in the latch extension of the spring latches and pull downward on the panel bases until all the latches disengage from the PSU rail. 25-23-61 SUBTASK 25-23-61-020-014 (3) Lower the inboard edge of the spacer panel while you pull out the outboard hook attachment of the panel from the beam detail extrusion.

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-030 (1) Adjust the panel to the necessary width. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-031 (2) Put the outboard hook attachments of the spacer panels into the beam detail air extrusion holes. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-032 (3) Push the inboard edge of the spacer panel upward until the spring latches engage the Passenger Service Unit (PSU) rail. SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-033 (4) Apply upward pressure to the panel base under the spring latches to fully engage the latches. NOTE: The latches will make a “click” sound when fully engaged.

D. Fixed Class Divider Header Removal

SUBTASK 25-24-10-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the header assembly [1] of the class divider: (a) Disconnect the electrical connectors, if applicable. (b) Do these steps to remove the curtain from the header assembly [1]: 1) Open the tiebacks to release the curtains [3]. 2) Remove the screw [5], washer [6], and nutplate [7] from one end of the header assembly [1]. CAUTION BE CAREFUL WITH THE CURTAINS. THE CURTAINS CAN BECOME DAMAGED AND DIRTY EASILY . 3) Move the sliders [4] out of the curtain track to remove the curtains [3] from the header assembly [1]. (c) If the header assembly [1] is installed with the bolt [8], do these steps (View B, Figure 401): 1) Remove the bolt [8], nut [10], and washers [9] on the each end of the header assembly [1] from the support clevis [11]. NOTE: When the header assembly is to be re-installed in the same location, record the location of the header assembly on the support clevis. 25-24-10 (d) If the header assembly [1] is installed with the quick release pin [13], do this step (View C, Figure 401): 1) Remove the quick release pin [13] from the support clevis [11] on the each end of the header assembly [1]. CAUTION BE CAREFUL WITH THE HEADER ASSEMBLY . THE HEADER ASSEMBLY CAN BECOME DAMAGED AND DIRTY EASILY . (e) Carefully remove the header assembly [1]. (f) To move the class divider to a new location, remove the nuts [12] that attach the support clevis [11] to the top of the stowage bin. 1) Remove the support clevis [11].

25-24-31-440-801Bin Assist Mechanism - ActivationPDF p. 525

2. Bin Assist Mechanism - Activation Figure 201

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions to activate the bin assist mechanism.

B. Activate the Bin Assist Mechanism

SUBTASK 25-24-31-440-001 (1) To activate the bin assist mechanism, do these steps: (a) Turn the inboard edge of the bin bucket up 1.5 in. (38.1 mm) or 3°arc (0 rad) minimum. NOTE: The bearing must clear the cam bracket which is not visible with the installed bucket. Turn the bin bucket more than 1.5 in. (38.1 mm) for the bearing to clear the cam bracket. (b) Use a hex wrench to tighten the bin assist screw. Tighten 20 in-lb (2 N·m) to 23 in-lb (3 N·m). NOTE: The head of the screw will be 0.33 in. (8.38 mm) from the outer edge of the cover plate when correctly installed. (c) Push the assist mechanism lever. NOTE: The assist will not activate until load is applied to the bucket. (d) Pull down on the threshold to apply load. 1) The bin assist will activate and start to pull the bin closed. 2) When assist is detected reapply load to threshold. 3) At the fully open position there should be two audible clicks. NOTE: The assist is now reset. (e) The assist mechanism lever will be in it's original position. NOTE: The bin bucket will turn freely, open and closed, without activation of the assist.

25-24-31-820-801Overhead Stowage Bin - Alternate Open MethodPDF p. 532

7. Overhead Stowage Bin - Alternate Open Method

A. General

(1) This task opens the overhead stowage bin with a malfunctioning latch. 25-24-31

B. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-1641 Lever - Stowage Bin Release Part #: J25001-5 Supplier: 81205

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-24-31-820-003 (1) If you can not open the stowage bin with the stowage bin handle, then do these steps to move the emergency release lever to release the stowage bin latch. NOTE: Usually the stowage bin handle will release one of the two latches. Use the emergency release lever to release the other latch. Pull down lightly at each end of the stowage bin, while you pull on the handle, to find which end is not released. Procedure 1 (Using the lever, SPL-1641) (a) Put the lever, SPL-1641 between the stowage bins above the latch. NOTE: Two to three inches below the top edge of the stowage bin is a good location to start. NOTE: The lever, SPL-1641 should work at all latch locations, but it is a tight fit at the slip joint locations. If you use it at a slip joint be careful not to damage the seal (make sure the lever, SPL-1641 does not have sharp edges). (b) Turn the lever, SPL-1641 to point toward the stowage bin you want to open. (c) Move the lever, SPL-1641 down and outboard, keeping it in contact with the lip of the stowage bin. At the same time, pull on the stowage bin handle (to release the other latch) and pull down on the stowage bin to open it. NOTE: You will feel the lever, SPL-1641 hit the emergency release lever. Push on the lever, SPL-1641 until the latch opens. NOTE: You must hold the emergency release lever until you open the bin. Usually the latch will close again if you release the emergency release lever before you open the bin. (d) Procedure 2 (When the lever, SPL-1641, is not available) NOTE: If the lever, SPL-1641, is available use it. It is the easier way to open the bin. 1) Open the stowage bin that is adjacent to the latch that will not release. NOTE: If you cannot open a stowage bin adjacent to the latch you want to release then you cannot use this procedure. You must use Procedure 1 above that uses the lever, SPL-1641. 25-24-31 2) Put your finger (not all fingers will fit) or a small object (such as a 1/4 inch drive deep socket or a Chapstick) in the channel at the edge of the stowage bin. Move it down the channel behind the latch and push down on the emergency release lever with it. At the same time, pull on the stowage bin handle (to release the other latch) and pull down on the stowage bin to open it. NOTE: You must hold the emergency release lever until you open the bin. Usually the latch will close again if you release the emergency release lever before you open the bin. SUBTASK 25-24-31-820-004 (2) Replace or adjust latch if it is necessary.

D. Overhead Stowage Bin Installation

SUBTASK 25-24-31-800-001 (1) Inspect the bin gap seal [2]. (a) Make sure that the bin gap seal [2] is serviceable and attached. SUBTASK 25-24-31-420-010 (2) Do these steps to connect the hardware to the applicable stowage bins: (a) For all stowage bins, do this step: 1) Install the bolt [17], washers [18], bushings [19], and nut [20] to connect the turnbuckle at the bottom outboard side of the stowage bin. (b) For the constant bin, do these steps: 1) Install the bolt [7], washer [8], and nut [9] to connect the diagonal strut at the top forward side of the stowage bin. 2) Install the bolt [3], washers [4], bushings [5], and nut [6] to connect the turnbuckles at the top aft side between the adjacent stowage bin. 3) Install the bolt [14], washers [15], and nut [16] to connect the turnbuckles at the top aft side of the aft stowage bin. (c) For the transition bin, do these steps: 1) Install the bin join plate [13], washers [12], nuts [11], and cotter pins [10] at the top of the transition bin to the termination bin. 2) Install the bolt [7], washer [8], and nut [9] to connect the diagonal strut at the top forward side of the stowage bin. 3) Install the bolt [3], washers [4], bushings [5], and nut [6] to connect the turnbuckles at the top forward and aft sides of the stowage bin. (d) For the termination bin, do these steps: 1) Install the bolt [14], washers [15], and nut [16] to connect the turnbuckles at the top end of the stowage bin. 2) Install the bin join plate [13], washers [12], nuts [11], and cotter pins [10] at the top of the transition bin to the termination bin. 3) Install the bolt [3], washers [4], bushings [5], and nut [6] to connect the turnbuckles at the top aft side of the stowage bin. 25-24-31-300-801Torque Tube Cover DoublerPDF p. 571

2. Torque Tube Cover Doubler (Figure 801)

A. General

(1) This task has the instructions for overhead stowage bin torque tube cover doubler installation. (2) The 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) thick aluminum torque tube cover doubler strengthens and prevents damage to the composite torque tube cover.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification A50038 Adhesive - Fast-setting, 2 Part Epoxy, Medium Viscosity BMS5-123 Type I Class 2 Clear B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 B50201 Wipe - Alcohol (Isopropyl Alcohol)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

D. Repair Procedure

SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-001 (1) Remove the screws adjacent to the worn area along the full length of the bin. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-002 (2) Install the torque tube cover and make sure that the holes in the doubler align with the bin inserts. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-003 (3) OPTIONAL: Clean the torque tube and doubler faying surfaces with alcohol wipes, B50201 or alcohol, B00130 then wipe dry before solvent evaporates. NOTE: Avoid the use of ketones. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-004 (4) OPTIONAL: Prepare the adhesive, A50038, mixing gun, and a new dispensing tip. Make sure that this mixes smoothly. NOTE: The adhesive, A50038 is a fast setting epoxy with the pot life of 4 minutes. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-005 (5) OPTIONAL: Apply the 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) adhesive bead in two places at the underside of the concave cross-section and outboard side angle. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-006 (6) Make sure that the torque tube cover doubler is installed correctly over the torque tube cover. 25-24-31 SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-007 (7) OPTIONAL: Use masking tape (3M or equivalent) on the doubler whilst the adhesive cures. Make sure that the tape is perpendicular to the doubler at equivalent distances along the length. NOTE: Make sure that only sufficient pressure is applied to hold the surfaces together. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-008 (8) Install the screws (BACS12FA3K5) and torque to 15 in-lb (1.7 N·m). SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-009 (9) OPTIONAL: Clean unwanted adhesive from the surfaces with alcohol wipes, B50201 or, alcohol, B00130 and a clean wiper. SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-010 (10) OPTIONAL: Make sure that the adhesive cures for 20-40 minutes before you remove the masking tape. 50% cure strength in 1 hour, 100% cure strength in 24 hours.

(a) Slide the center latch [42] through the hole in the center of the bin. NOTE: Make sure the arrow molded into the back of the center latch [42] is pointed toward the upper edge of the bin. (b) Align each support bracket [44] with its associated insert on the back of the center latch [42]. (c) Install the screws [43] to install the support brackets [44] but do not tighten. (d) Slide the torque tube [41] through the bin hole and end latch hole. (e) Slide the torque tube [41] into the square hole in the center latch [42]. (f) Slide the universal [40] through the same hole and into the torque tube [41]. (g) Install the universal [40] into the morse taper [38]. (h) Install the cap screw [36] and washer [37] to the morse taper [38] but do not tighten. (i) Do the same to install the opposite torque tube [41] and universal [40]. (j) Make sure the center latch [42] is centered in the bin. 519-999 1) Torque the screws [43] on the support brackets [44] to 15 in-lb (1.69 N·m). 378-518 2) Torque the screws [43] on the support brackets [44] to 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m) 378-999 (k) Make sure both end latches are latched. 1) Insert a screwdriver into the open strike in the end latch and push toward the face of the bin. A black tab will pop up that indicates the mechanism is latched. (l) Use a slide hammer, COM-13625 to gently tap the universal [40] into the morse taper [38] and into the mating part of the end latch. NOTE: Use care not to scratch the surface of the torque tube [41] or the inside of the bin face. 1) Remove any looseness by very gently rotating the torque tube [41] toward you (as you face the bin). (m) Do the same to the opposite universal [40] and torque tube [41]. (n) Make sure the door latches correctly. 1) Pull the handle in the center latch assembly. The bin should unlatches satisfactorily. 2) If the bin does not unlatch satisfactorily, gently unseat the universal [40] from the morse taper [38] and start again from step (3) (k) above. (o) Keep the torque tube [41] from rotating and tighten the cap screws [36] on both universals [40] to 15 in-lb (1.7 N·m). (p) Install the torque tube cover [35] with the screws [33] and screws [34]. 519-999 1) Torque screws [33] and screws [34] to approximately 15 in-lb (1.69 N·m). 25-24-36 378-518 2) Torque screws [33] and screws [34] to approximately 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m).

A. General

(1) This procedure provides the instructions to install the attendant panel flipguard assembly. NOTE: This procedure starts with only the housing and the brackets for the flipguard screw on the panel. Bypass the steps that do not apply to the degree of assembly necessary.

Reference Description Specification A50571 Adhesive - General Purpose - Loctite 425 B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 C00047 Adhesive - Silicone RTV, 1 Part, Sealant Primer MIL-A-46106 C00048 Primer - PR 1200 Prime Coat Adhesion Promoter G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A) G01659 Swab - Cotton Or Rayon, (Disposable) G02439 Brush - Nylon Bristle G50314 T ape - Masking BAC5034-4 Type VII Class 2

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

E. Prepare for the Flipguard Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 25-25-11-010-003 (1) Do this task: Attendant's Panel with LCD Touch Panel - Removal, TASK 25-25-11-000-802. F . Install the Flipguard Assembly SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-007 WARNING CLEANING SOLVENT IS COMBUSTIBLE AND VAPOR MAY BE TOXIC. AVOID PROLONGED BREATHING OF VAPOR AND PROLONGED OR REPEATED CONTACT WITH SKIN. AVOID CONTACT WITH EYES. CLEAN PARTS IN WELL-VENTILATED AREA AND USE APPROVED SAFETY EQUIPMENT . 25-25-11 378-999 (Continued) (WARNING PRECEDES) CAUTION OBSERVE PRECAUTIONS FOR HANDLING ELECTROSTATIC SENSITIVE DEVICES (ESD). (1) Do these tasks to install the flipguard damper [3]: (a) Clean the area with alcohol, B00130, and a cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Let it dry for 15 minutes. (b) Apply a PR 1200 prime coat adhesion promoter, C00048 with a brush, G02439. 1) Let it dry for 15 minutes. 2) Wipe off the excess primer. (c) Apply the adhesive, C00047, in the housing cavity. (d) Install the flipguard damper [3] in the housing cavity over the adhesive and compress the flipguard damper [3] in place with a cotton swab, G01659. 1) Wipe off the excess adhesive around the flipguard damper [3] with a clean cotton swab, G01659. a) Let it dry for 1 hour at 131°F (55°C) or air dry for 24 hours. SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-008 (2) Do these tasks to prepare the flipguard assembly: NOTE: The flipguard assembly consists of the flipguard [4] and the torsion springs [5]. (a) Insert one torsion spring [5] in the flipguard [4] with long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View A1, Figure 403). (b) Hold the torsion spring [5] with your thumb and remove the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733. (c) Adjust the torsion spring [5] into place with the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View A1, Figure 403). (d) Insert a No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, halfway into the flipguard [4] to seal the torsion spring [5] into place. (e) Adjust the torsion spring [5] with the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View A2, Figure 403). (f) Insert the second torsion spring [5] into the flipguard [4]. (g) Insert the No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, all the way into the flipguard [4] to seal the second torsion spring [5] into place (View A3, Figure 403). SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-009 (3) Do these tasks to install the flipguard assembly: NOTE: The flipguard assembly consists of the flipguard [4] and the torsion springs [5]. (a) Apply masking tape, G50314, on the housing to protect the surface of the housing. (b) Position the flipguard assembly on the housing (View A4, Figure 403). 1) Insert the torsion springs [5] into the housing holes. If necessary, adjust the torsion springs [5] into place with long-nosed pliers, STD-3733. (c) Insert the flipguard screw [1] into the housing and the flipguard assembly (View A5, Figure 403). 25-25-11 378-999 (Continued) 1) Use the screw [1] to push the No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, out from the flipguard assembly. (d) Use a brush, G02439, to apply Loctite 425 adhesive, A50571, on the two outside threads of the flipguard screw [1]. (e) Install the flipguard nut [2] on the flipguard screw [1]. 1) Use a hex wrench, STD-7012, or 1/8 inch socket, STD-20883, to tighten the nut [2] to 1.80 in-lb (0.20 N·m). a) Use a second hex wrench, STD-7012, or 1/8 inch socket, STD-20883, to prevent the screw [1] from turning. SUBTASK 25-25-11-210-001 (4) Make sure that when you open and release the flipguard [4], it springs back to the closed position. SUBTASK 25-25-11-020-012 (5) Remove the masking tape, G50314, from the surface of the housing. SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-010 (6) Do this task: Attendant's Panel with LCD Screen - Installation, TASK 25-25-11-400-802.

25-25-12-000-801Attendants' Seat RemovalPDF p. 623

2. Attendants' Seat Removal (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

B. Attendants' Seat Removal

SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-001 (1) Remove the Headrest [4]. To remove it, pull on it. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). (a) Remove the mounting Bolts [5] and Washers [8] that attach the inertia reel bracket of the seat belt to the wall. SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-002 (2) Open the storage compartment door below the seat and remove the mounting Bolts [2] and Washers [6]. SUBTASK 25-25-12-010-001 (3) Do these steps to open the lower seat back: (a) Open the seat pan a small distance. (b) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back. To open it, pull it away from the upper seat back. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). (c) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back. (d) Pull the seat back out and down. SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-003 (4) Remove the mounting Bolts [3] and Washers [7] that are behind the lower seat back. SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-004 (5) Remove the Attendant seat [1]. SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-001 (6) If installed, remove life vest located in the life vest container. NOTE: N/A this step if seat is not being transported offsite. (This includes any mode of transportation) SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-002 (7) Route Attendant seat [1] to shop if necessary.

25-25-12-400-801Attendants' Seat InstallationPDF p. 624

3. Attendants' Seat Installation (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

B. Attendants' Seat Installation

SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-001 (1) Put the Attendant seat [1] in its position. (a) If the stowage box of the Attendant seat [1] has a cut-out, make sure that the cut-out is on the outboard side. NOTE: The cut-out provides additional clearance for the girt bar of the adjacent entry door. SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-002 (2) Open the storage compartment door below the seat and install the mounting Bolts [2] and Washers [6]. SUBTASK 25-25-12-010-002 (3) Do these steps to open the lower seat back: (a) Open the seat pan a small distance. (b) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back. To open it, pull it away from the upper seat back. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). (c) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back. (d) Pull the seat back out and down. SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-003 (4) Install the mounting Bolts [3] and Washers [7] that go behind the lower seat back. SUBTASK 25-25-12-410-001 (5) Close the lower seat back. SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-004 (6) Attach the inertia reel bracket of the seat belt to the wall with its Bolts [5] and Washers [8]. SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-005 (7) Install the Headrest [4]. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-003 (8) If required for overwater operation, install one each life vest in life vest container.

25-25-12-200-801Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment InspectionPDF p. 627

2. Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment Inspection (Figure 601) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

B. Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment Inspection

SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-001 (1) Make sure that the seat belts and the shoulder harness are not worn or damaged. SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-002 (2) Do these steps to examine the top mounting bolts [5] of the seat: (a) Remove the headrest [4]. NOTE: The headrest is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). 1) To remove it, pull on the headrest [4]. (b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [5] that attach the bracket for the inertia reels to the wall are not loose. (c) Make sure that the mounting bolts that attach the inertia reels of the shoulder harness to the bracket are not loose. (d) Install the headrest. SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-003 (3) Do these steps to examine the middle mounting bolts of the seat: (a) Do these steps to open the lower seat back: 1) Open the seat pan a small distance. 2) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back. NOTE: The fabric flap is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro). a) To open it, pull the fabric flap away from the upper seat back. 3) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back. 4) Pull the seat back out and down. (b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [3] that attach the seat to the wall are not loose. (c) Close the lower seat back. SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-004 (4) Do these steps to examine the lower mounting bolts of the seat: (a) Open the storage compartment door. 25-25-12 (b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [2] that attach the seat to the wall are not loose. (c) Close the storage compartment door. SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-005 (5) Do these steps to examine the lower attachment points for the seat belts: (a) Pull the seat cushion away from the attachment points for the seat belts. (b) Make sure that the bolts are tight. SUBTASK 25-25-12-200-001 (6) Do these steps to inspect the pivot points of the seat pan: (a) Open the seat pan. (b) Hold the seat pan near its back corner and shake the seat pan to make sure that it is not loose. (c) Make sure that the seat pan has no obvious cracks.

25-25-12-710-801Attendants' Seat Bottom CheckPDF p. 630

3. Attendants' Seat Bottom Check (Figure 601)

A. General

(1) This task is an inspection of the attendants' seat bottom, referred to in this procedure as the seat pan.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-25-12-710-001 (1) Push the seat pan fully down (open) and release it. Make sure the seat pan retracts to its fully up (closed) position without aid. SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-006 (2) Do these steps to examine the pivot points of the seat pan: (a) Open the seat pan. (b) Hold the seat pan near its back corner and shake the seat pan to make sure it is not loose. (c) Make sure the seat pan has no obvious cracks.

(c) Release the shoulder harness. 1) Make sure the shoulder harness retracts.

(a) Isopropyl alcohol, B00130 (IPA) : 1) Make sure that the area where you will use this solvent has good air flow, and remove ignition sources. NOTE: This solvent has a high flash point and is a lower risk. It can be safely used with the usual precautions with electrical power on the airplane. (b) Vertrel MCA solvent, B50005 or HFE 71DE solvent, B50003 (c) Limonene solvent, B00634 (d) citra-safe solvent, B50225 (e) citra-safe solvent, B50226 NOTE: These solvents are not flammable.

E. Floor Covering Removal Standard Method

SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-006 (1) Remove the entry area mat. (a) Remove the threshold plate from the edge of the mat. (b) If it is necessary, remove or loosen the threshold to release the mats. SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-007 (2) Remove the entry and service area floor covering. (a) Release the mat from the edge thresholds. (b) If it is necessary, remove the sealant around the mat. (c) Carefully release the mat from the tape that holds the mat to the waterseal. 25-27-21 (d) If you replace the entire area, do these steps to remove the waterseal: 1) Pull the strips of 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, or 3M 8663 tape, G51482, from the floor. 2) Remove fillet seal from the edges of the sidewall. F . Floor Covering Removal Alternate Method SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-008 (1) Remove the entry area mat. (a) Remove the fasteners from the doorway threshold and flight deck threshold. (b) Remove the girt bar latch fittings (TASK 25-66-02-000-801). (c) Remove or loosen the doorway threshold and flight deck threshold to release the mats. CAUTION OBEY THESE PRECAUTIONS. IF YOU IGNORE THESE PRECAUTIONS, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT WILL OCCUR. 1) Be careful when you remove the mat; do not damage the waterseal when you use a skin wedge, STD-1178, or equivalent. (d) Remove the plastic aisle threshold with a skin wedge, STD-1178, or equivalent. SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-009 (2) Do these steps, when entry and service area floor covering with monuments is installed: (a) Separate the edge of the mat from the tape. (b) If it is necessary, remove the sealant around the mat. (c) Pull the mat upward from the tape and toward the monument wall. NOTE: This area is where the mat will be trimmed. (d) Put a protective strip fabric, G00088, or equivalent between the waterseal and mat. NOTE: The waterseal can be damaged if the fabric, G00088, or equivalent is not used to protect it. (e) Carefully cut the mat that is adjacent to the monument walls. NOTE: This is to start the mat removal. (f) Release the rest of the mat. (g) Carefully pull the mat from under the monument wall. SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-010 (3) If you replace the entire area, do these steps to remove the waterseal: (a) Pull the strips of 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, 3M 8663 tape, G51482, or moisture barrier tape, G51340 from the floor. (b) If it is necessary, remove the fillet seal from the edges of the sidewall.

WARNING SOLVENT MATERIALS USED TO CLEAN CONTAIN POISONOUS INGREDIENTS. PREVENT CONTACT OF THESE MATERIALS WITH SKIN OR EYES. USE SOLVENT MATERIALS WITH SUFFICIENT AIR FLOW OR RESPIRATOR MASKS. (1) If the waterseal is not removed and replaced, prepare the waterseal surface for the mat. (a) Examine the waterseal for cuts, tears abrasions, or other signs of deterioration. (c) If it is necessary, clean the waterseal with oil-free cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 91 solvent, B01011. (d) Clean the sealant from the edge thresholds. 1) Do not let the solvent get on the waterseal or on the undisturbed sealant. SUBTASK 25-27-21-840-002 (2) If the waterseal is removed, prepare the floor panels for the waterseal. (a) Clean the floor panels, do these steps: 1) Apply Series 91 solvent, B01011, with clean oil-free cotton wiper, G00034. 2) Rub the surface to remove the soil. 3) Use clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it evaporates. (b) Protect the floor tracks from corrosion (SRM 51-20-01). (c) Keep the floor panels clean prior to applying the waterseal.

E. Floor Covering Installation

SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-001 (1) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the waterseal: CAUTION DO NOT CUT THE TAPE AGAINST A FLOOR PANEL, SEAT TRACK, ATTACH FITTING, OR OTHER TAPE. CORROSION AND STRUCTURAL DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE EQUIPMENT . (a) Apply moisture barrier tape, G50179, to all floor panel seams in the galley and lavatory areas, extending 20 in. (51 cm) aft of the forward wet area and 20 in. (51 cm) forward of the aft wet area. 25-27-21 (b) Apply 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663 tape, G51482, or moisture barrier tape, G51340, across the entire area perpendicular to the center line of the airplane. 1) Make sure that there is a minimum of a 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) overlap of each strip. (c) Push the tape down firmly in all areas. (d) Apply sealant, A00247, or sealant, A02315, to the edges, cracks, and small holes. 1) Make sure that the waterseal and adjacent structure has a complete seal. (e) Clean the surface of the waterseal with an cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 91 solvent, B01011. 1) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it evaporates. F . Floor Covering Installation Standard Method SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-006 (1) Install the entry area mat. (a) Install the entry monuments as necessary. NOTE: The galleys, lavatories, and partitions that edge the sides of the entry mat must be installed before the mat. (b) Cut the mat to the correct dimensions. (c) Apply carpet tape, G01288, 6.0 in. (15.2 cm) wide, on the floor surface with no gaps. NOTE: Avoid running the tape over the raised areas and floor panel inserts. The direction of the tape is optional. NOTE: Adhesive Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, has displayed better results in countering mat buckling. Recommended to use this tape in areas of observed buckling. NOTE: Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, has stronger adhesion properties making it more difficult to remove, care should be taken in its removal. 1) Keep carpet tape, G01288, at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) from the mat edges. (d) Apply RTV6708 adhesive, A50030, for faying surfaces on the trim as well as sealing all the cracks and small holes. NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to RTV6708 adhesive, A50030. (e) Clean the bottom side of the mat with an cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 91 solvent, B01011, that will contact the waterseal. 1) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it evaporates. (f) Put the mat in the correct location and push firmly on the tape. (g) Apply adhesive, A00930, at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.35 in. (8.89 mm) wide, between the edge of the mat and floor panel. NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to adhesive, A00930. (h) Put the edges in the edge thresholds before the sealant starts to get hard. SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-008 (2) Put the carpet in the edge threshold for the mats. 25-27-21 SUBTASK 25-27-21-390-007 (3) Apply adhesive, A00930, to the thresholds. NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to adhesive, A00930. SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-009 (4) If it is necessary, install or tighten the mat to carpet thresholds. SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-010 (5) Install the threshold plate on the edge of the mat and drain trough. (a) Install the fasteners with adhesive, A00930, or RTV 108 adhesive, A50414. 1) Apply the adhesive below the head of the fastener. SUBTASK 25-27-21-390-005 (6) If it is necessary, install the floor brackets for the escape slide adjacent to the entry and service doors (TASK 25-66-02-400-801). SUBTASK 25-27-21-390-006 (7) Install the thresholds over the edge of the mat at the drain trough. (a) Apply adhesive, A00930, along the joint between the galley mat and drain trough (Figure 401 sheet 3). NOTE: The adhesive, A00027, is optional to adhesive, A00930. (b) Install the fasteners with adhesive, A00930, or RTV 108 adhesive, A50414. 1) Apply the adhesive below the head of the fastener. (c) Make sure that there is a water-tight surface. SUBTASK 25-27-21-160-003 (8) Remove the excess sealant.

G. Floor Covering Installation Alternate Method

SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-002 (1) Install the entry area mat. (a) Do these steps to cut the mat to the correct size: 1) If it is necessary, precut a slit, centered between the monument walls. NOTE: Use the template or remove mat as a pattern to precut the new mat. NOTE: Cutting a slit in the mat prepares the mat for future removal. 2) Cut the mat to extend 0.15 in. (3.81 mm) to 0.35 in. (8.89 mm) past the galley walls. NOTE: The mat will be located under the galley wall and the foam seals. NOTE: Do not cut the mat around the galley partition fittings. The fittings will be installed on top of the mat. 3) If a closet is installed, cut the mat to extend under the closet installation. 4) Cut the mat to fit around the forward fixed lavatory. 25-27-21 CAUTION DO NOT USE NITTO P-55 (A BRAND OPTION FOR G50155) OR P-55B (A BRAND OPTION OF G50156) DIRECTLY ON FLOOR PANEL SURFACES. THESE TAPES WILL DELAMINATE FLOOR PANEL SURFACES WHEN THEY ARE REMOVED. (b) Apply carpet tape, G01288, 6.0 in. (15.2 cm) wide, on the floor surface leaving no gaps. NOTE: Do not let the tape go over the raised areas and floor panel inserts. The direction of the tape is optional. 1) Keep the tape at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) from the mat edges. (c) Apply RTV6708 adhesive, A50030, for faying surfaces on the slit edges of the mat running adjacent to the monuments. NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to RTV6708 adhesive, A50030. (d) If it is necessary, seal all the cracks and small holes. (e) Clean the bottom side of the mat with an cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 91 solvent, B01011, that will contact the waterseal. 1) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it evaporates. (f) Put the mat in the correct location and push firmly on the tape. (g) Apply adhesive, A00930, at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.35 in. (8.89 mm) wide, between the edge of the mat and floor panel. NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to adhesive, A00930. (h) Put the edges in the edge thresholds before the sealant starts to get hard. SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-003 (2) Put the carpet in the edge threshold for the mats. SUBTASK 25-27-21-390-008 (3) Apply adhesive, A00930, to the thresholds. ALL (c) Turn the water shutoff valve [2] in the galley to the OFF position. (d) Open the faucet to release the water pressure and drain some of the water. (e) Close the faucet when the water stops. F . Galley Water Filter Replacement SUBTASK 25-31-10-900-001 (1) Remove the water filter. (a) Put a container, STD-193, or cotton cloth, G50316, below the filter case [3] to absorb spilled water. (b) Loosen the vent screw [6] (where applicable) and let the water drain from the pressure vessel. (c) Remove the clamp [5] at the top of the filter case [3]. 25-31-10 (d) Remove the filter cartridge [4] from the filter case [3]. (e) If it is necessary, examine the cartridge seal and housing gasket. NOTE: Contact the galley manufacturer for the part numbers of the seal or gaskets. SUBTASK 25-31-10-960-001 (2) Replace the water filter. (a) Clean the inner part of the filter case [3] with a clean cotton cloth, G50316. (b) Install a clean filter cartridge [4]. 1) Flush the new filter cartridge [4] at the time of installation. NOTE: This is done by running water through the filter at full flow from the service top for three minutes or until water runs clear. (c) Install the clamp [5]. 1) Make sure that the clamp [5] is installed in the correct position and head of the wingnut does not cause the interference with the cart. (d) Tighten the wingnut on the clamp [5]. (e) Open the water shutoff valve [2]. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-24-1147 (f) Set the GALLEY switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the ON position. 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-24-1147 (g) Set the CAB/UTIL switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the ON position. ALL (h) Open the vent screw [6] at the top of the filter case [3] to bleed air. (i) Close the vent screw [6]. (j) Pressurize the potable water system. 1) Do this task: Potable Water System - Activation, TASK 38-42-00-800-802. (k) Open the faucet. (l) Make sure that there are no leaks around the water filter assembly [1].

SUBTASK 25-31-11-210-001 (1) Do a check of the water barrier on the galley floor for damage. (a) If it is necessary, do this task: Entry and Service Area Floor Covering - Installation, TASK 25-27-21-400-801. SUBTASK 25-31-11-100-001 (2) Clean the galley mat on the floor in the galley area with solvent, B00083. SUBTASK 25-31-11-350-001 (3) If it is necessary, repair the galley mat. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-001 (4) Move the galley inboard near its final position. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-139 (5) Connect the ground strap [4] to the ground stud [3]. SUBTASK 25-31-11-760-003 (6) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the top of the galley and ground stud [3] (SWPM 20-20-00). (a) Use the non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. (b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 Ohms (2.5 milliohms) or less. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-007 (7) Connect the electrical connectors [8] in the ceiling above the galley. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-017 (8) If exit light is installed, put the wires through the panel before the galley is in its final position. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-002 (9) Put the galley into its final position. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-011 (10) If necessary, install the stabilizer [14]. (a) Put the stabilizer [14] below the galley. (b) Attach the stabilizer [14] with the bolts [15] and washers [16]. 1) Torque the bolts [15] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). (c) Seal the stabilizer [14] with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930. ALL 25-31-11 SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-012 (11) Connect the water supply. (a) Connect the water supply connection [5] at the top of the galley. (b) Install the shroud [6] on the water supply connection [5] with plastic tie straps [7]. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-003 (12) If it is necessary, loosely install the bolts [9], washers [10], and shims [11] at the four floor hard points. NOTE: This will prevent galley movement while the floor seals are installed. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-085 (13) If necessary, install the floor seals and bond them with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930. SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-004 (14) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [9] and install the bolts [9], washers [10], and shims [11] at the four floor hard points. NOTE: Install the shims as necessary. The shim installation could not be more than 3 shims per attachment fitting. (a) Tighten the bolts [9] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m). SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-005 (15) Install the hard point coverplates and seal with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930. SUBTASK 25-31-11-820-002 (16) Attach the tie rod [1] to the attachment fitting on the top of the galley. (a) If it is necessary, adjust the tie rod [1] to the correct length. 1) Adjust only the end of the assembly without the lockwasher and lockwire. NOTE: The end of the tie rod with the lockwasher and lockwire attached at the fitting on the fuselage. 2) Make sure that the thread of the tie rod [1] blocks the inspection hole in the body of the tie rod [1]. 3) Tighten the jamnut. (b) Install the quick release pin [2] at the galley end of the tie rod [1]. (b) Remove the equipment from the galley before doing the procedure. (c) Remove the necessary access panels from the galley to complete the task. (d) Remove the necessary trim panels from the galley to complete the task. F . Galley Removal SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-013 (1) Disconnect the water supply at the connection at the top of the galley. (a) Get access through the applicable access panel in the top of the galley. (b) Disconnect the water connection [4] above the top of the galley. 25-31-21 SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-004 (2) Through the lower access panel, loosen the clamp [5], then disconnect the drain line [6]. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-005 (3) Remove the tie rod [9]. (a) Remove the quick-release pin [10] that attaches the tie rod [9] to the galley lug fitting [11]. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-006 (4) To remove the galley floor hard points, do these steps: (a) Remove the coverplate on the floor hard points. (b) If it is necessary, remove the grease from the attachment fitting to get access to the fasteners. (c) Remove the bolts [12], washers [13], and shims [14] at the four hard point locations. NOTE: Keep the shims for the galley installation. Record the quantity of shims for a given location when you remove the shims. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-009 (5) Do these steps to remove the stabilizer [21] fitting: (a) Remove the bolts [15], washers [16], and nuts [17] at the bearing block [18]. (b) Remove the bearing block [18]. (c) Remove the bolts [19] and washers [20] at the stabilizer [21]. (d) Remove the stabilizer [21]. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-042 (6) If it is necessary, move the galley out slightly for easier access to the electrical connectors [1] and ground stud [3]. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-011 (7) Disconnect the electrical power at the connections above the galley. (a) Disconnect the electrical connectors [1]. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-012 (8) Disconnect the ground strap [2] from the ground stud [3] at the top of the galley. SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-010 (9) Lift up and remove the galley. SUBTASK 25-31-21-030-002 (10) If it is necessary, remove the seat track fittings at the seat track locations.

C. Sealant Installation Procedure

SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-001 (1) FOR LAVATORIES WITH BI-FOLD DOORS; Do these steps to apply sealant to the threshold area: (a) Remove the bi-fold door [5]. (b) If necessary, remove the threshold [2] installed bellow the lavatory [1] door. (c) Clean the areas that will be sealed (TASK 51-31-00-160-801). (d) Apply a bead of sealant [3] of RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 around the bi-fold door pivot hole [11] (TASK 51-31-00-390-801). (e) Install the threshold [2]. (f) Remove the excess RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 from the threshold [2]. (g) Apply a sealant [4] around the interior edges of the threshold [2] with RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). (h) Install the bi-fold door [5]. SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-002 (2) FOR LAVATORIES WITHOUT BI-FOLD DOORS; 25-40-01 Do these steps to apply sealant to the threshold area: (a) If necessary, remove the threshold [2] installed below the lavatory [1] door. (b) Clean the areas that will be sealed (TASK 51-31-00-160-801). (c) Install the threshold [2]. (d) Apply a sealant [4] around the interior edges of the threshold [2] with RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-003 (3) Apply sealant to the lavatory cover plates [6]: (a) Apply fay surface sealant [7] to the cover plates [6] with adhesive, A00027, adhesive, A00930 or RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-801). (b) Install the cover plates [6] to the lavatory foor fittings [8]. SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-004 (4) Install the new floor sealant [3] between panels and floor and the wall adjacent to the airplane door. (a) Clean the area where the sealant will be applied (TASK 51-31-00-160-801). (b) Bond the floor seal with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930 (TASK 51-31-00-390-801). NOTE: Seal on the wall panel seam must be continuous approximately 6 in. (152 mm) from the floor. SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-005 (5) Apply one of these sealants to all exposed fasteners, gaps, or seams less than 6 in. (152.4 mm) up from the floor. NOTE: Select the color to match the adjacent surfaces. It is possible to use RTV 108 adhesive, A00635, for all variations. • RTV 102 adhesive, A50067 • RTV 103 adhesive, A50119 • RTV 106 adhesive, A00081 • RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 • RTV109 sealant, A50011.

25-40-08-200-801Lavatory Waste Compartment InspectionPDF p. 745

2. Lavatory Waste Compartment Inspection (Figure 601) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044

B. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure

006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044; LAVATORIES WITH AN INNER WASTE COMPARTMENT DOOR SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-001 (1) Do these steps for lavatories with an inner waste compartment door and an outer waste compartment door to make sure the waste compartment doors close correctly: (a) Open the outer waste compartment door. (b) Open the inner waste compartment door and release it. 1) Make sure the springs close the inner door without your help. (c) Make sure the inner door is not bent or blocked such that it does not close fully. It must close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire. (d) Close the outer waste compartment door. 1) Make sure the latch holds the outer door closed. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044; LAVATORIES WITHOUT AN INNER WASTE COMPARTMENT DOOR SUBTASK 25-40-08-800-001 (2) Do these steps for lavatories that do not have an inner waste compartment door to make sure the outer waste compartment door closes correctly. (a) Open the waste compartment door. (b) Make sure the door and seals are not damaged or blocked so that it does not fully close. NOTE: The door must closely tightly to make sure that it can contain a fire. NOTE: Some doors have a door plate with springs behind it instead of a visible seal. (c) Close the waste compartment door. (d) Make sure the waste compartment door latches correctly and holds the door securely closed. 25-40-08 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-416

C. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure

SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-003 (1) Do these steps to make sure the door closes tightly: (a) Pull the latch at the bottom of the door to open the door. (b) Push around the edge of the door plate on the inner side of the door. 1) Make sure the door plate moves quickly back to its initial position. NOTE: There are springs behind the door plate. These springs compress when the door is closed. (c) Do a visual check of the door plate on the inner side of the door for general condition. (d) Close the door. (e) Do these steps to make sure the latches are fully engaged: 1) Push the door in the upper and lower latch area. 2) Make sure the lower latch is parallel to the door. NOTE: If you can easily see red on the lower latch, the latches are not fully engaged. 417-999

D. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure

SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-004 (1) Do these steps for lavatories with an inner waste compartment door and an outer waste compartment door to make sure the waste compartment doors close correctly: (a) Open the outer waste compartment door. NOTE: The latch is at the bottom of the door. (b) Open the inner waste compartment door and release it. 1) Make sure that the springs close the inner door without your help. (c) Make sure the inner door is not bent or blocked such that it does not close fully. It must close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire. (d) Close the outer waste compartment door. 1) Make sure the latch holds the outer door closed. ALL

E. Waste Compartment Flap Inspection Procedure

SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-002 (1) Do these steps to make sure the waste compartment flap operates correctly: (a) Push the waste compartment flap open. (b) Release the waste compartment flap and make sure it closes fully. (c) Make sure the waste compartment flap is not bent such that it does not close fully. It must close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire.

(b) Open the junction box access panel [21]. 25-40-11 (c) Remove the sealant where the junction box access panel [21] attaches to the lavatory [1] and at the seam between the panels. 25-52-00-200-803Forward Cargo Compartment Liner InspectionPDF p. 815

2. Forward Cargo Compartment Liner Inspection NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task inspects all the liners in the forward cargo compartment. (2) It is important that all of the fasteners, seams, and punctures are sealed correctly to keep the amount of oxygen in the compartment to a minimum.

B. References

Reference Title 21-32-05 P/B 401 CARGO COMPARTMENT BLOWOUT PANELS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION 25-00-00-300-801 Crushed-Core and Sandwich Panel Repair (P/B 801) 25-52-01-300-802 Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves (P/B 801) 25-52-01-300-806 Neoprene Coated Cargo Liner Repair (P/B 801) 25-52-01-300-807 Silicone Impregnated Liner Repair (P/B 801) 25-52-01-300-808 Permanent Repair for the Contour of the Ceiling Shroud (P/B 801) 25-52-01-340-801 Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners (P/B 801) 25-52-01-350-801 Loose or Damaged T ape Repair (P/B 801) 25-52-06-000-801 Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal (P/B 401) 25-52-06-400-801 Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation (P/B 401) 25-52-09-000-801 Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal (P/B 401) 25-52-09-400-801 Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation (P/B 401) 25-52-10-000-801 Cargo Floor Panel - Removal (P/B 401) 25-52-10-400-801 Cargo Floor Panel - Installation (P/B 401) 25-52-16-000-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal (P/B 401) 25-52-16-400-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Installation (P/B 401) 25-52-17-000-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal (P/B 401) 25-52-17-400-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation (P/B 401) 25-52-00

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 121 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 122 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-001 (1) Make sure that there is no loose or damaged tape at the joints for the ceiling liner, sidewall liner or bulkhead liner. (a) If there is loose or damaged tape, replace the tape (TASK 25-52-01-350-801). SUBTASK 25-52-00-211-001 (2) Make sure that the ceiling liners, sidewall liners, bulkhead liners and panels, blowout panels and floor panels do not have any cuts, tears, cracks, or holes. (a) If there are cuts, tears, cracks or holes found on the blowout panel, replace the blowout panel (PAGEBLOCK 21-32-05/401). SUBTASK 25-52-00-200-006 (3) If damage is found, examine the non-honeycomb liners for damage as follows: NOTE: These damage limits apply to all the non-honeycomb liners. These are the ceiling panels and shrouds, sidewall, forward bulkhead and aft cargo compartment liners. These damage limits do not apply to cracks along the contour of the ceiling shroud in the forward cargo compartment. (a) Cuts that are longer than 36 in. (91 cm) are not repairable. (b) L-shaped tears that are longer than 9 in. (23 cm) on either side are not repairable. (c) Holes that are over 1.5 in. (3.8 cm) in diameter are not repairable. (d) Cracks within 2 in. (5 cm) of other damage, or from any panel edge are not repairable. SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-006 (4) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do the applicable task to repair the liner: (a) Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners, TASK 25-52-01-340-801. (b) Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves, TASK 25-52-01-300-802. NOTE: T ask Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves, TASK 25-52-01-300-802 for cracks along the contour of the ceiling shroud. This can be the ceiling shroud in the forward cargo compartment or other areas with contours. (c) Neoprene Coated Cargo Liner Repair, TASK 25-52-01-300-806. (d) Silicone Impregnated Liner Repair, TASK 25-52-01-300-807. SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-007 (5) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the applicable liner as follows: (a) Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801 and Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-09-400-801. (b) Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal, TASK 25-52-06-000-801 and Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation, TASK 25-52-06-400-801. (c) Cargo Floor Panel - Removal, TASK 25-52-10-000-801 and Cargo Floor Panel - Installation, TASK 25-52-10-400-801. 25-52-00 SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-007 (6) If damage is found, examine the contour of the ceiling shroud in the cargo compartment for damage as follows: (a) Make sure that cracks are at least 2 in. (5 cm) away from other damage and from the panel edge on all sides. NOTE: These damage limits only apply to cracks or cuts along the bend of the shroud. For damage to the flat parts of the shroud, use the damage limits and repair instructions for non-honeycomb liners. SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-002 (7) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do this task to repair the lining: (a) Permanent Repair for the Contour of the Ceiling Shroud, TASK 25-52-01-300-808. (b) Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves, TASK 25-52-01-300-802. SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-003 (8) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the liner (Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801 and Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-09-400-801). SUBTASK 25-52-00-200-005 (9) If damage is found, examine the nomex honeycomb panels for damage as follows: (a) For panels with core damage, there must be at least 0.5 in. (1.3 cm) of undamaged core around the damaged area. SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-003 (10) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do the following steps: NOTE: Dents on the cargo compartment bulkhead panel assembly that shows no damage to the integrity of the facesheet (e.g. holes, cracks, damaged fiber) are structurally acceptable and repair is not necessary. (a) Do this task: Crushed-Core and Sandwich Panel Repair, TASK 25-00-00-300-801. (b) Apply a flame-resistant patch (Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners, TASK 25-52-01-340-801). NOTE: Multiple damage sites may be covered with longer strips in lieu of multiple shorter strips. NOTE: Patch may be applied over fastener locations by removing the fastener and reinstalling through the patch. NOTE: Splices in the patch system require a minimum of one (1) inch overlap. SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-004 (11) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the applicable liner as follows: (a) Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-16-000-801 and Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-16-400-801. (b) Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-17-000-801 and Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-17-400-801.

C. Blowout Panel Inspection

SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-006 (1) Make sure the blowout panel is fully engaged between the retaining ring and the rectangular seal. (a) Do these steps to put the blowout panel in the correct position if it is not fully engaged: 1) Remove the screws and washers that attach the grill to the frame. 2) Remove the grill. 3) Loosen the applicable bolts that attach the retaining ring to the frame in the area where the blowout panel came out. 4) Make sure that the blowout panel do not have any cuts, tears, cracks, or holes. a) If there are cuts, tears, cracks or holes found on the blowout panel, replace the blowout panel (PAGEBLOCK 21-32-05/401). 5) Put the blowout panel in the position between the retaining ring and the rectangular seal. 6) Tighten the bolts that attach the retaining ring to the frame. 7) Install the screws and washers to attach the grill to the frame. SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-007 (2) Make sure the grill is firmly attached and is aft of the blowout panel.

SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-004 (10) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do the following steps: NOTE: Dents on the aft cargo compartment bulkhead panel assembly that shows no damage to the integrity of the facesheet (e.g. holes, cracks, damaged fiber) are structurally acceptable and repair is not necessary. (a) Do this task: Crushed-Core and Sandwich Panel Repair, TASK 25-00-00-300-801. (b) Apply a flame-resistant patch (TASK 25-52-01-340-801). NOTE: Multiple damage sites may be covered with longer strips in lieu of multiple shorter strips. NOTE: Patch may be applied over fastener locations by removing the fastener and reinstalling through the patch. NOTE: Splices in the patch system require a minimum of 1 in. (3 cm) overlap. SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-005 (11) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the liner (Aft Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-19-000-801 and Aft Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-19-400-801).

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-52-00-100-001 (1) Use these standard tools and equipment. (a) high capacity vacuum, STD-1068 (wet and dry) (b) Drum - 30 or 55 gallon capacity, mounted on casters (c) Hose Assembly - 6 foot length, 1 1/2-inch ID; with a swivel connection to the pump - Graco Model 206-266 siphon tube (d) Hose - 50 foot length, 3/8-inch ID, 2250 PSI working pressure with 3/8-inch pipe fitting at each end - Graco Model 207-831 (e) Portable Airless Pump - Graco bulldog Model 207-463; Hydraclean Pressure with 7 gpm output, 1200 psi working pressure, 10:1 ratio pump on pneumatic cart Model 208-156, with regulator assembly 206-199; Graco Incorporated, 60-11th Ave NE, Minneapolis MN 53440 (f) Portable airless pump, STD-7824 - Regulated airless, 50 - 1200 psi working pressure, 3 - 8 gpm output. SUBTASK 25-52-00-110-001 (2) Use one of these alkaline emulsion solvents: (a) Calla 301 cleaner, B00014 (b) Cee Bee A-410B solvent, B00432 (c) Cee Bee 280 cleaner, B00005 (d) Dubois C-1102 cleaner, B00013 (e) GMC 528B cleaner, B00003 (f) Hydrex 09 solvent, B00433 (g) Metaclean AC solvent, B00434 (h) Oakite 204 cleaner, B00008 (i) Pace B-82 alkaline cleaner, B00017 25-52-00 (j) TEC Formula No. 1 cleaner, B00016 (k) TEC 86-2 cleaner, B00335 (l) Turco Jet Clean C cleaner, B00012 (m) Turco Jet Clean E cleaner, B00325 NOTE: The following cleaners are optional to GMC 528B cleaner, B00003: • cleaner, B00402 • Cee Bee 280 cleaner, B00005 • Oakite 204 cleaner, B00008 • Calla 301A cleaner, B00015. F . Prepare to Clean SUBTASK 25-52-00-860-001 (1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. SUBTASK 25-52-00-910-001 (2) Do this task: Static Grounding, TASK 20-40-11-910-801. SUBTASK 25-52-00-020-001 CAUTION YOU MUST REMOVE ALL COMPONENTS THAT ARE NOT RESISTANT TO DAMAGE FROM THE SOLVENTS OR WATER. DAMAGE TO SOME COMPONENTS CAN OCCUR IF THEY BECOME WET WITH THE SOLVENTS OR WATER. (3) Remove all of the blankets and components that are not resistant to damage from solvents and water. SUBTASK 25-52-00-950-001 CAUTION APPLY THE MASKING TAPE AND PAPER TO ALL AREAS THAT YOU WILL NOT CLEAN. YOU MUST OBEY THE MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS. THESE CLEANERS HAVE HIGH CONCENTRATION LEVELS AND CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PAINT OR CAN CAUSE THE CORROSION OF METAL SURFACES (4) Cover the areas that you will not clean. Use Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 with one of the these protective materials: NOTE: This includes protection of all the lubricated or waxed surfaces and the latches and fittings. • polyethylene film, G00252 • barrier material, G00253 • Angier 30 paper, G00258.

G. Clean the cargo compartment

SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-001 (1) Remove the dirt, fluids, and the other loose material with a high capacity vacuum, STD-1068 as necessary. 25-52-00 SUBTASK 25-52-00-110-002 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . CAUTION DO NOT USE SOLVENTS THAT ARE NOT ON THE LIST OF CONSUMABLE MATERIALS. IF YOU USE OTHER SOLVENTS, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT COULD OCCUR. (2) Apply the solution of alkaline cleaner and water to the compartment with the airless pump, STD-7824 or the Graco bulldog portable airless pump. (a) Let the solution soak for 5 minutes, but do not let it dry. (b) Apply more solution as necessary to keep the surfaces wet. SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-002 (3) Remove the solution and the materials loosened by the solution with the high capacity vacuum, STD-1068. SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-003 (4) Do steps (2) and (3) again until the compartment is clean, as necessary. SUBTASK 25-52-00-170-001 (5) Flush the compartment with clean water. (a) Use pressure to apply the water. SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-004 (6) Remove the water with the high capacity vacuum, STD-1068, as necessary. SUBTASK 25-52-00-750-001 (7) Do this pH check for the compartment as follows with litmus paper, G50412: (a) Do a pH check of the clean water. (b) Do a pH check of the water which remains caught in the compartment. 1) Do this check in more than one area. (c) Compare the pH check of the clean water with the pH of the water still caught in the compartment. (d) Make sure the pH in step (b) is not more than 1 pH unit of the pH in step (a). 1) If necessary, flush the compartment again with clean water. SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-005 (8) Dry the area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. SUBTASK 25-52-00-620-001 (9) Do this task: Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802.

H. Put the Airplane Back in its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 25-52-00-950-002 (1) Remove all of the masking tape and paper. 25-52-00 SUBTASK 25-52-00-410-001 (2) Install the equipment you removed. SUBTASK 25-52-00-910-002 (3) Remove the static ground. SUBTASK 25-52-00-860-002 (4) If it is necessary, do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.

25-52-01-350-801Loose or Damaged Tape RepairPDF p. 833

2. Loose or Damaged Tape Repair

A. General

(1) It is not necessary to remove the liners from the airplane for this repair.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification A50465 T ape - Cargo Lining, 3 inches wide BMS5-146 Type I Class 1 Grade A B00090 Solvent - Inhibited Trichloroethane 1,1,1 MIL-T-81533 B00093 Solvent - T etrachloroethylene (Perchloroethylene) ASTM D4081 G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 121 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 122 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 141 Aft Cargo Compartment - Left 142 Aft Cargo Compartment - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 25-52-01-020-003 (1) Remove or discard all loose or damaged tape. SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-004 CAUTION DO NOT LET THE SOLVENT TOUCH PLASTICS, CONTROL CABLES, LUBRICATED AREAS, PLASTIC DECALS, OR PAINTED AREAS OR MARKINGS THAT ARE NOT SKYDROL RESISTANT . THE SOLVENT WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE ITEMS. (2) Clean the damaged area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00093, or solvent, B00090. SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-005 (3) Dry the area with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034, before the solvent dries. 25-52-01 SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-006 (4) Clean the area again fully to remove the dirt, oil, paint, and other unwanted materials. NOTE: A clean surface is necessary for a good bond. SUBTASK 25-52-01-420-003 WARNING DO NOT PUT TAPE ON THE SMOKE DETECTOR TUBES OR THE FIRE EXTINGUISHER OUTLET TUBES. THE SMOKE DETECTOR AND THE FIRE EXTINGUISHER SYSTEM WILL NOT SENSE A FIRE IF THERE IS TAPE ON THE TUBE OR OUTLETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT APPLY TAPE ON THE BLOWOUT PANELS OR CAP STRIPS ON THE CEILING LINER. IN THE AFT CARGO COMPARTMENT , DO NOT APPLY TAPE BETWEEN THE CEILING LINER AND CAP STRIP ALONG THE CEILING CENTERLINE. THE JOINT GIVES A VENT PATH FOR AIR FLOW IF A DECOMPRESSION OCCURS. IF THE PRESSURE RELIEF FUNCTION OPERATES INCORRECTLY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Apply T ape, A50465, to the area. NOTE: Apply the tape with the minimum number of joints in it. Do not apply tape between the ceiling liner and aft bulkhead liner. The tape at this joint should be only on the ceiling liner. In both the forward and aft cargo compartments, the aft bulkhead does not need tape applied to its joints. NOTE: Do not use the old tape again. If you use the tape again, it will not have a satisfactory bond. NOTE: Do not apply the tape to the blowout panels or cap strips on the ceiling liner. NOTE: Do not apply tape over installed placards. Applying tape over placards makes them illegible. (a) Make sure that the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion. (b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or higher, to help promote good adhesion. (c) If it is necessary to use short pieces of tape, make a minimum overlap of 0.50 in. (12.70 mm). (d) Push the tape firmly to make sure that there is a good bond. NOTE: If the surface of the tape is smooth and does not have air bubbles, there is a good bond.

25-52-01-340-801Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved LinersPDF p. 834

3. Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners (Figure 801)

A. General

(1) There are four alternatives for permanent repairs. It is only necessary to use one of the four alternatives. 25-52-01

B. References
